artworks.title: Alpheus and Arethusa
artworks.description: Maratta paints the river-god in pursuit — Alpheus of Elis hunting the Naiad whose spring on Ortygia he will still seek beneath the sea.

artworks.title: Alpheus and Arethusa
artworks.description: Restout's academic canvas pairs the god and the nymph at the moment of flight — Alpheus as desire that will not stop at the shoreline of Sicily.

artworks.title: Alpheus and Arethusa
artworks.description: A Metropolitan Museum print from the Metamorphoses cycle shows Alpheus closing on Arethusa — the river that Ovid says mingles with her Sicilian waters.

artworks.title: Arethusa Pursued by Alpheus in a Wooded Landscape
artworks.description: The wooded chase again names the god: Alpheus as the hunter whose love drives the nymph underground and across the Ionian to Syracuse.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid makes Alpheus the river who will not release Arethusa — the Elian god whose waters, the poets say, still seek her fountain under the sea.

popCulture.title: Alpheus (deity)
popCulture.description: River-god of Elis, son of Oceanus and Tethys — famed for his pursuit of Arethusa to Ortygia.
